title: Daimler-Benz, the maker of Mercedes, is now available to you
what: Daimler-Benz of Stuttgart builds Mercedes-Benz cars and is one of the world's biggest makers of trucks and buses. Its new S-Class saloon went into production in December 1979. The Deutsche Bank, Kuwait and the Mercedes-Automobil-Holding are its big shareholders. Gerhard Prinz has been chairman of the board of management since January 1980.
why: The listing beat. The arc runs from the solid car maker through Reuter's conglomerate, Chrysler and back to a pure luxury car maker.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_W126 (read 2026-10-03); Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 1981, https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/1981.xhtml?oid=4910808 (read 2026-10-03); https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daimler-Benz (list of chairmen, read 2026-10-03); Daimler-Benz Annual Report 1985, 'Change in Shareholder Structure', https://bib.kuleuven.be/files/ebib/jaarverslagen/Daimler-Benz_1985.pdf (read 2026-10-03)

title: Mercedes launches the 190, its first compact car
what: Daimler-Benz has put the Mercedes 190 and 190 E on the market, the first compact car of the brand. Daimler has spent eight years and a fortune developing it, with advanced suspension and lightweight high-strength steel.
why: The 190 (W201) broadened the range and fed the volume growth of the mid-1980s that made Daimler a stock-market darling. The month's +19% in dollars came partly from a firmer mark.
source: Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 1982 ('Market launch of 190 and 190 E'), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/1982.xhtml?oid=4910821 (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_W201 (read 2026-10-03)

title: Daimler takes control of Dornier as foreigners pile into German shares
what: After buying all of the engine maker MTU from MAN in February, Daimler-Benz signed contracts in April and May, with help from the state government of Baden-Württemberg, to buy a majority of the aerospace company Dornier, about 66% for around 500 million marks. Foreign investors are buying German blue chips on the back of a strong economy and rising profits, and Daimler is their favourite; its price rose by about a quarter between the end of April and the end of June.
why: The game's series has no May 1985 price (the printed quote was doubtful), so the +27% of June is an April-to-June move. MTU and Dornier were the first steps outside cars; Dornier came with family quarrels and veto rights that cost Daimler another 570 million marks later.
source: Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 1985 ('MTU becomes subsidiary', 14 February 1985; 'Daimler-Benz acquires Dornier shares', 23 April and 15 May 1985), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko.xhtml?oid=4910873&viewType=list (read 2026-10-03); Der Spiegel 31/1995, https://www.spiegel.de/spiegel/print/d-9205712.html (read 2026-10-03); Die Zeit, 'Börsen-Report: Daimler ist Spitze', 30 August 1985, https://www.zeit.de/1985/36/daimler-ist-spitze (read 2026-10-03); data/manual/mercedes.csv header (1985-05 left out) (read 2026-10-03)

title: Foreign buyers return and Daimler leads the rebound
what: German share indices rose about 10% in less than three weeks in February as foreign investors stopped selling and began to buy again, followed by German insurers. The dollar has stabilised and interest rates are falling. Reports say Daimler-Benz is close to taking over the aerospace and defence group MBB, as the federal government wants.
why: Relief rally after the crash; Daimler rebounded more than most (+27% in dollars, about +30% in marks; Siemens +17%).
source: Die Zeit, 'Markt-Report: Aktien wieder hoffähig', 19 February 1988, https://www.zeit.de/1988/08/aktien-wieder-hoffaehig (read 2026-10-03); Die Zeit, 'Markt-Report: Ein Lichtblick', 12 February 1988, https://www.zeit.de/1988/07/ein-lichtblick (read 2026-10-03); Die Zeit, 'Daimler/MBB: Perversion', 12 February 1988, https://www.zeit.de/1988/07/perversion (read 2026-10-03)

title: The 'Germany boom': Daimler soars after the Wall falls
what: Since the opening of the Berlin Wall in November, foreign investors have been buying German blue chips, seeing West German industry as the main winner of the new markets in the East. The DAX reached a new post-war high before Christmas. In November the government allowed Daimler-Benz to take over MBB from 1 January, making it Germany's largest technology and defence group; Daimler also raised 1.9 billion marks by issuing new shares at 460 marks.
why: Reunification euphoria. Daimler's +34% in December (about +27% in marks, the rest a weaker dollar) partly recovered a November dip caused by the rights issue. In May and June Daimler had reorganised into a holding company over Mercedes-Benz AG, Deutsche Aerospace (DASA) and AEG.
source: Die Zeit, 'Mehr Optimismus bei Ausländern', 1 December 1989, https://www.zeit.de/1989/49/mehr-optimismus-bei-auslaendern (read 2026-10-03); Die Zeit, 'Schöne Bescherung', 29 December 1989, https://www.zeit.de/1990/01/schoene-bescherung (read 2026-10-03); Die Zeit, 'Daimler/MBB: Prinzip Hoffnung', 24 November 1989, https://www.zeit.de/1989/48/prinzip-hoffnung (read 2026-10-03); Daimler-Benz Annual Report 1989, 'Allocation of Earnings' (capital increase of November 1989), https://bib.kuleuven.be/files/ebib/jaarverslagen/Daimler-Benz_1989.pdf (read 2026-10-03); Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 1989 ('Mercedes-Benz AG formed', 29 June 1989), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/1989.xhtml?oid=4912361 (read 2026-10-03)

title: The new A-Class tips over in the 'elk test'
what: On 21 October the new Mercedes A-Class, the brand's first small car, rolled onto its side and roof in a swerving test by the Swedish magazine Teknikens Värld. Daimler-Benz responded that it will fit its electronic stability programme ESP to every A-Class as standard, so far a feature of luxury cars. At the end of the month the Asian financial crisis caused a crash on stock markets worldwide.
why: An embarrassment for the quality brand at the worst moment; the -19% month mixes the elk test with the Asian-crisis crash of 27-28 October.
source: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elchtest (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_Asian_financial_crisis (read 2026-10-03)

title: Daimler-Benz and Chrysler agree to merge
what: On 7 May Daimler-Benz and the American car maker Chrysler signed a contract to merge into DaimlerChrysler, a deal valued at about 38 billion dollars, the largest cross-border merger ever. Schrempp calls it a merger of equals. The new company will build Mercedes, Chrysler, Jeep and Dodge cars.
why: The defining bet of the Schrempp era. In practice a takeover of Chrysler; it destroyed value for nine years and ended with Chrysler's sale in 2007.
source: Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 1998 ('Merger: contract signed with Chrysler', 7 May 1998), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/1998.xhtml?oid=4912914 (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Group (read 2026-10-03)

title: DaimlerChrysler shares start trading
what: The merger was completed on 17 November and the new DaimlerChrysler share began trading in Frankfurt and New York. Daimler-Benz shareholders had approved the deal with 99.9% in September. Stock markets have recovered from the summer's Russian crisis.
why: Name change in the game: Daimler-Benz becomes DaimlerChrysler. The +18% came with the general autumn rebound after the Russian crisis; it was close to the high point of the Chrysler years.
source: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daimler-Benz (merger on 17 November 1998, read 2026-10-03); Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 1998 (Extraordinary General Meeting, 17 September 1998), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/1998.xhtml?oid=4912914 (read 2026-10-03)

title: DaimlerChrysler buys into Mitsubishi's truck business
what: On 14 March DaimlerChrysler bought 43% of Mitsubishi Fuso Truck and Bus, the truck business split off from Mitsubishi Motors in January. It adds a big Asian maker to DaimlerChrysler's truck business, which already includes Mercedes-Benz and Freightliner.
why: Of Schrempp's Asian adventures only the trucks lasted: Fuso became part of Daimler Truck.
source: Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 2003 ('Commercial vehicles: principal shareholder of Mitsubishi Fuso', 14 March 2003), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/2003.xhtml?oid=4913233 (read 2026-10-03)

title: No more money for Mitsubishi
what: On 22 April the boards of DaimlerChrysler decided at an extraordinary meeting not to take part in a new capital increase for Mitsubishi Motors, which is in trouble after a quality scandal. DaimlerChrysler is pulling back from its Asian alliance; in May it also restructured its alliance with Hyundai.
why: The world company falls apart: DaimlerChrysler had bought 34% of Mitsubishi Motors for about 2 billion dollars in 2000; the Hyundai stake was sold in August 2004 and the last Mitsubishi shares in 2005.
source: Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 2004 ('DaimlerChrysler withdraws from Mitsubishi Motors', 22 April 2004; Hyundai, 12 May and 16 August 2004), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/2004.xhtml?oid=4913323 (read 2026-10-03); https://www.encyclopedia.com/social-sciences-and-law/economics-business-and-labor/businesses-and-occupations/daimler-ag (2000 Mitsubishi stake, read 2026-10-03)

title: Schrempp quits and the shares jump
what: On 28 July DaimlerChrysler said Jürgen Schrempp will step down at the end of the year. Dieter Zetsche, who has turned Chrysler around with models such as the 300C, will take over. Investors had criticised the lagging share price and weak profits at Mercedes; the shares rose almost 10% on the day.
why: The market voted on Schrempp: the departure of the merger's architect was the best news in years (+20% month).
source: NBC News, 'DaimlerChrysler CEO Schrempp to step down', 28 July 2005, https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna8737805 (read 2026-10-03); Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 2005 ('Board of Management chairman: Zetsche follows Schrempp', 28 July 2005), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/2005.xhtml?oid=4913367 (read 2026-10-03)

title: Chrysler is sold to Cerberus
what: On 14 May DaimlerChrysler agreed to sell 80.1% of Chrysler to the private-equity firm Cerberus in a deal valued at 7.4 billion dollars, keeping 19.9%. Chrysler lost 1.5 billion dollars in 2006 and announced 13,000 job cuts in February. DaimlerChrysler's shares rose on the news.
why: The divorce: nine years after the 'marriage made in heaven', Daimler paid to be rid of Chrysler. The remaining stake was given up in 2009.
source: NBC News, 'Chrysler Group to be sold for $7.4 billion', 13-14 May 2007, https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna18645179 (read 2026-10-03); Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 2007 ('Spinoff of the Chrysler Group', 14 May 2007), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/2007.xhtml?oid=4913464 (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Group (read 2026-10-03)

title: DaimlerChrysler becomes Daimler
what: On 4 October an extraordinary shareholders' meeting approved renaming DaimlerChrysler AG as Daimler AG. The sale of Chrysler to Cerberus was completed on 3 August. The company now concentrates on Mercedes-Benz cars and on trucks, where it is the world's biggest maker.
why: Name change in the game. The share was near a post-merger high just before the financial crisis (the -79% worst stretch starts here).
source: Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 2007 ('DaimlerChrysler AG becomes Daimler AG', 4 October 2007; 'Cerberus acquires majority of Chrysler Group', 3 August 2007), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/2007.xhtml?oid=4913464 (read 2026-10-03)

title: Abu Dhabi buys 9.1% of Daimler
what: On 22 March Daimler announced a capital increase of about 10%, sold entirely to Aabar Investments of Abu Dhabi, which becomes its largest shareholder with 9.1%. The new money strengthens Daimler in the crisis; it has put German truck plants on short-time work.
why: Gulf money returned to Daimler, as Kuwait's had in 1974; the deal marked the bottom of the crisis for the shares.
source: Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 2009 ('Aabar Investments (Abu Dhabi) becomes major Daimler investor', 22 March 2009; short-time working, 11 March 2009), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/2009.xhtml?oid=4913607 (read 2026-10-03); Al Jazeera, 'Daimler boosted by UAE investment', 23 March 2009 (headline, via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)

title: Daimler walks away from Chrysler as markets rebound
what: On 27 April Daimler, Chrysler, Cerberus and the US pension guarantee agency agreed that Daimler gives up its remaining 19.9% of Chrysler and pays into Chrysler's pension funds, ending all ties. Chrysler is heading for bankruptcy. Stock markets rallied strongly in April on hopes that the worst of the crisis is over.
why: +42%, the best month in the series: a relief rally from the March low plus the final break with Chrysler.
source: Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 2009 ('Daimler reaches agreement over split with Chrysler', 27 April 2009), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/2009.xhtml?oid=4913607 (read 2026-10-03); BMW Group Annual Report 2009, 'Capital Market Activities' (markets recovered from March lows), https://bib.kuleuven.be/files/ebib/jaarverslagen/BMW_2009.pdf (read 2026-10-03)

title: German car shares race ahead
what: German car makers are booming as the economy recovers; in July Daimler raised its profit target for 2010. In September stock markets rallied worldwide and German car shares led the DAX. The euro rose from 1.27 to 1.36 dollars during the month. BMW gained 32 percent in the month and Daimler 30 percent.
why: +30% in dollars: about 21% in euros plus the euro's rebound after the spring's Greek crisis. German auto shares rose 56% in 2010.
source: BMW Group Annual Report 2010, 'Automobile stocks boost DAX' (Prime Automobile index +56.5% in 2010), https://bib.kuleuven.be/files/ebib/jaarverslagen/BMW_2010.pdf (read 2026-10-03); Times of Malta, 'Daimler raises 2010 earnings target', 28 July 2010 (headline, via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); FRED DEXUSEU, data/raw/fred/DEXUSEU.csv (read 2026-10-03)
changed: note to the writer addressed: BMW added (text and tag)

title: A new S-Class for Mercedes
what: Mercedes-Benz presented the new S-Class, its flagship luxury saloon, at a lavish premiere on 15 May. Daimler is also renewing its compact cars.
why: A new flagship in a good year for the share, which rose strongly in 2013.
source: Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 2013 ('New S-Class unlocks new dimensions in luxury, comfort and efficiency', 15 May 2013), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/2013.xhtml?oid=188893673 (read 2026-10-03)

title: Daimler sells its Tesla stake
what: Daimler sold its remaining shares in the electric car maker Tesla for a reported 780 million dollars. It took almost 10% of Tesla in May 2009, when Tesla was a small private company, and sold part of the stake to its shareholder Aabar later that year. Tesla supplied batteries and motors for electric versions of the Smart and the Mercedes B-Class.
why: A good trade at the time, and a missed opportunity in hindsight: the stake would have been worth many times more by 2020.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (Daimler stake, read 2026-10-03); Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 2009 ('Daimler takes a stake in Tesla', 19 May 2009; Aabar, 13 July 2009), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/2009.xhtml?oid=4913607 (read 2026-10-03); The Detroit News, 'Daimler sells 4% Tesla stake', 22 October 2014 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)

title: Volkswagen's diesel cheating shakes German car makers
what: On 18 September US authorities accused Volkswagen of using software to cheat diesel emissions tests. VW said about 11 million cars worldwide carry the software, its chief executive Martin Winterkorn resigned, and its shares lost a third within days. Investors now ask whether other diesel makers have similar problems.
why: Start of the diesel-scandal years that later reached Daimler itself (recalls 2017, US fine 2020).
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volkswagen_emissions_scandal (read 2026-10-03)

title: Diesel recall and cartel allegations
what: Daimler said on 18 July it will update the software of more than 3 million Mercedes diesel cars in Europe to cut emissions. Days later reports said German car makers including Daimler had for years coordinated technology in secret working groups, including on diesel exhaust cleaning.
why: The diesel issue moved from Volkswagen to Mercedes; Daimler later paid a US fine for emissions cheating.
source: The Guardian, 'Mercedes recalls 3m diesel cars over emissions concerns', 19 July 2017; Bloomberg, 'German Carmakers Can't Catch a Break as Next Scandal Looms Large', 21 July 2017 (headlines via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Group (2020 Clean Air Act fine, read 2026-10-03)

title: Geely's founder becomes Daimler's biggest shareholder
what: Li Shufu, founder of the Chinese car maker Geely, which owns Volvo, has bought 9.69% of Daimler, making him the largest single shareholder.
why: With BAIC's 5% (2019, later about 10%) Chinese owners held almost a fifth of the company, which became a political issue in Washington in 2026.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Group (read 2026-10-03)

title: Ola Källenius takes over as trade war worries hit car shares
what: Dieter Zetsche handed over to Ola Källenius on 22 May after 13 years as chief executive, and Daimler is restructuring its organisation. In May the US raised tariffs on Chinese goods and threatened Mexico with tariffs, hitting car shares worldwide. Daimler paid its dividend of 3.25 euros a share in May. Tesla fell 22% to a three-year low, hit harder than other car makers because it is building a factory in Shanghai and counts on selling many cars in China.
why: About 7 points of the -21% are the dividend (prices exclude dividends); the rest is trade-war fear and a run of profit warnings over diesel costs.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dieter_Zetsche (read 2026-10-03); electrive.com, 'Daimler restructures as Zetsche hands reins to Källenius', 22 May 2019 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); The Japan Times, 'Carmakers see $17 billion wiped out by Trump's Mexico threat', 1 June 2019 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); data/out/mercedes.json (dividend in May 2019) (read 2026-10-03); The Detroit News, 'Tesla hammered hardest by China tariff fears', 13 May 2019 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (Gigafactory Shanghai from January 2019, read 2026-10-03); data/out/tsla.json (read 2026-10-03)

title: Daimler spins off its truck business
what: Daimler Truck, the world's biggest maker of heavy trucks, began trading on the Frankfurt stock exchange on 10 December as an independent company, after Daimler's shareholders voted for the spin-off on 1 October. What remains of Daimler is the Mercedes-Benz car and van business, and it plans to rename itself after its brand.
why: The final step of the 'back to cars' story that began in 1996. The game's price series is adjusted for the spin-off.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Group (read 2026-10-03); Daimler Truck press release 'Daimler Truck launched on stock exchange as an independent company', 10 December 2021, https://www.daimlertruck.com/en/newsroom/pressrelease/daimler-truck-launched-on-stock-exchange-as-an-independent-company-51850448 (via Google News, read 2026-10-03); CNBC, 'Daimler shareholders vote in favor of truck division spinoff', 1 October 2021 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); data/src/universe.ts (spin-off factor) (read 2026-10-03)

title: Daimler becomes Mercedes-Benz Group
what: On 1 February Daimler AG officially changed its name to Mercedes-Benz Group AG. Chief executive Ola Källenius wants investors to value the company as a luxury brand, selling fewer cars at higher prices, as it shifts deeper into electric cars.
why: Name change in the game. The 'fewer cars, more luxury' strategy paid off until Chinese demand for German luxury cars collapsed in 2024-2026.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Group (read 2026-10-03)

title: Mercedes promises a 3-billion-euro buyback
what: Presenting its 2023 results on 22 February, Mercedes-Benz announced a share buyback of up to 3 billion euros, despite warning of 'exceptional' uncertainty ahead. The shares rose 5% that day. It also slowed its plan to sell only electric cars and will keep updating its petrol models.
why: Cash returns kept the share up for a while (+17% month) before the China slump.
source: CNBC, 'Mercedes shares climb 5% on share buyback, despite exceptional uncertainty ahead', 22 February 2024; Reuters, 'Mercedes-Benz delays electrification goal, beefs up combustion engine line-up', 22 February 2024 (headlines via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)

title: China's slump forces a profit warning
what: On 19 September Mercedes-Benz cut its margin forecast for cars because sales in China, its largest market, are weakening fast. The shares slumped. Other European car makers also issued warnings this month.
why: The China problem that dominates the arc from 2024 to 2026.
source: Reuters, 'Mercedes-Benz cuts margin outlook on weak Chinese market, shares fall', 20 September 2024; Bloomberg, 'Mercedes Slumps After Warning China Rout Is Hurting Profits', 19 September 2024 (headlines via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)

title: BMW's warning drags Mercedes down
what: On 16 June BMW cut its profit forecast for 2026 because of a faster downturn in China and the effects of the war with Iran. European car shares fell the next day on fears that others will follow; Mercedes, already weak, lost another 3%. Mercedes is preparing further cost cuts.
why: The -18% month has no single Mercedes announcement; it reflects the sector-wide derating on China and energy costs.
source: Investing.com, 'European car stocks fall on BMW profit warning contagion fears; Mercedes down 3%', 17 June 2026 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/bmw-warns-significant-profit-decline-104414505.html (read 2026-10-03); just-auto.com, 'Mercedes Cost-Cutting Faces Labour Scrutiny', 22 June 2026 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)

title: Mercedes falls to a new low on China and Washington
what: Mercedes-Benz shares hit a 52-week low of about 40 euros on 30 September, down a third this year. Its sales in China collapsed by 30% in the second quarter. A US Senate bill against Chinese-owned car makers would have covered Mercedes, which is almost 20% owned by Chinese investors, until a senator said at the end of the month that Mercedes will be exempted. The company is buying back shares and plans a voluntary severance scheme.
why: Late in the arc the luxury strategy is under pressure from China on two fronts: lost sales there and its Chinese shareholders in Washington.
source: AD HOC NEWS, 'Mercedes-Benz Dodges Washington's China Crosshairs as Buyback Engine Idles Toward October Test', 1 October 2026, https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/unternehmensnachrichten/mercedes-benz-dodges-washington-s-china-crosshairs-as-buyback-engine-idles-toward-october-test/70210921 (read 2026-10-03); Carscoops, 'Mercedes Will Avoid US Ban, Despite 20% Chinese Ownership', https://www.carscoops.com/2026/10/mercedes-benz-avoids-chinese-car-ban-us/ (read 2026-10-03)
